summary: The @gyomu/concept package serves as the primary engine for modeling the architectural structure of TypeScript projects. It automates the transformation of raw file system information into high-level conceptual models and generates developer-facing documentation.
responsibilities: Analyze project source code to resolve package boundaries and dependency graphs.
Synthesize raw directory and file data into persistent architectural concepts.
Orchestrate the automated generation and localization of technical documentation.
Validate structural conceptualizations against project metadata and defined schemas.
Provide infrastructure for caching and retrieving project-wide conceptual models.

capabilities.name: Package Conceptualization
capabilities.description: Translates TypeScript project structures into comprehensive architectural models, identifying key components and external dependencies.

capabilities.name: Documentation Generation
capabilities.description: Automates the assembly, localization, and rendering of project README files based on analyzed project data.

capabilities.name: Directory Analysis
capabilities.description: Examines file system structures to produce metadata-rich representations of directory contents and internal hierarchies.

designDecisions: Uses a layered approach to separate the concerns of architectural discovery from document synthesis.
Employs a model-based strategy where file system state is converted into persistent, versionable concepts before consumption.
Leverages external schema and analysis packages to maintain consistency across the @gyomu ecosystem.
Favors automated generation processes that rely on source-of-truth project analysis to ensure documentation remains synchronized with code.
usageGuidance: Use the package-level builders to initialize architectural models from existing local project roots.
Integrate the documentation generator into your project's CI/CD pipeline to ensure README files reflect the latest architectural state.
Prioritize defining clear directory boundaries to help the analysis engine produce more granular and accurate conceptual models.
